headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Semantic Kernel’s broad egress and file access can amplify Haystack outputs into external actions, while shared MCP surfaces create injection and conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and Semantic Kernel also calls MCP servers, so a shared bridge exists. Semantic Kernel’s plugin/function-calling pattern and file surfaces mean attacker-controlled content from Haystack outputs could be treated as instructions if passed through without provenance checks. This is inferred from docs-only profile data, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF Haystack output is forwarded into an MCP tool call without provenance tagging, injection risk is present.
IF Semantic Kernel parses Haystack-generated text as instructions, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Add provenance labels before any MCP handoff.
Strip or escape instruction-like text from Haystack outputs.
Require allowlisted tool names for Semantic Kernel.
Insert a human review step for first-run prompts.
requires-engineering: add structured message schemas between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and Semantic Kernel can read/write application-defined files plus send context to model providers and MCP/OpenAPI tools. If they share a workspace or file handoff, application context and anonymous usage statistics can flow into external services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty is kept at medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or file handoff, leakage risk is active.
IF Semantic Kernel forwards file contents to a model provider or MCP tool, data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent.
Disable file ingestion for sensitive folders.
Review outbound destinations in Semantic Kernel plugins.
Rotate any exposed plugin credentials.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Semantic Kernel can read and write files, while Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress. Even though Haystack’s write capability is not documented, both can mutate shared external resources through MCP or APIs, and Semantic Kernel supports multiple instances with shared memory-store state. That creates a realistic conflict pathway in default orchestration, though not the highest-risk write/write case.
conditions: IF both agents target the same MCP server or shared memory store, concurrent mutation conflicts can occur.
IF Semantic Kernel instances run in parallel against shared state, last-writer-wins behavior can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate MCP endpoints per agent.
Use per-agent namespaces in shared stores.
Serialize writes with a lock or queue.
Disable parallel runs during shared-state updates.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency/version checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can generate retrieved facts, and Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs. If Semantic Kernel treats Haystack results as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream API calls or file writes. Because Semantic Kernel has broad egress and file write capability, the blast radius can be irreversible, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes Haystack output without verification, cascading error risk is active.
IF downstream plugins perform external actions based on retrieved facts, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require citation checks before actioning results.
Add a verification step against source documents.
Gate external actions behind approval.
Log provenance for every retrieved claim.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds for tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack’s profile only shows anonymous usage statistics, while Semantic Kernel handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials and may send application context to third-party providers. No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supported. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow, not one agent alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Semantic Kernel plugins to external model providers, compliance review is required.
IF Haystack is configured to collect more than anonymous usage statistics, the compliance surface changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review provider DPAs before enabling plugins.
Disable telemetry where possible.
Document retention settings for shared outputs.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing controls.
